judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is exact on all four problems, and I checked it in worksheet.tex and verify.json rather than off the rendered page. Problem 5 prints two demands — 'Simplify $i^{18}$. State the remainder you used when you divided the exponent by 4' — and verify.json id 5 is a lone eval (I**18 -> -1); the remainder 2 is nowhere in the verification data even though answer_key.pdf computes it explicitly ('18 = 4 * 4 + 2, remainder 2'). Problem 6 adds 'Say in one sentence what happened to the imaginary parts of the first two numbers' to a single eval; problem 7 adds 'say in one sentence why the answer has no imaginary part' to a single eval; problem 12 adds 'say in one sentence why the product came out with real coefficients' on top of its expand and zeros entries. None is declared manual, and machine_observation confirms gate_chain_manual_flags: false. final_response.md states the overclaim in as many words: 'Nothing is flagged manual.' The mathematics is entirely sound — I recomputed all twelve independently with SymPy and got 7+3i, 5-7i, 21+12i, 13+13i, -1, 3+3i, 29, 7-24i, 1-i, 3+-2i, 9+7i, and x^2-10x+26 with zeros 5+-i, all matching the key. REJECT is correct.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 7 and problem 12 are the same idea taught twice at different altitudes: (5+2i)(5-2i)=29 shows a conjugate pair collapsing to a real number, then the synthesis problem builds (x-(5+i))(x-(5-i)) and asks why the coefficients came out real. The key closes the loop arithmetically rather than by assertion — 'their sum (5+i)+(5-i)=10 and their product (5+i)(5-i)=26 are both real, and those are precisely the coefficients the expansion produces'.

The key's solution to problem 12 groups the factors as ((x-5)-i)((x-5)+i) and reads it as a difference of squares, which is a genuinely better method than blind FOIL and shows the student where the conjugate structure went.

The declared trap on problem 7 is the correct one for this topic and it is machine-checked as distinguishable: 21 is exactly what (5+2i)(5-2i) becomes if i^2 is read as +1, and the key's grading note names it.

Problem 11 is staged deliberately — 'Multiply the first two factors, simplify to standard form, and only then multiply by the third' — and the key follows the same staging, which is what stops an unsimplified i^2 being carried into the second product.

No skeleton repeats across the twelve: sum, difference, monomial times binomial, binomial times binomial, single power of i, three-term chain, conjugate pair, square, sum of two powers, quadratic with negative discriminant, triple product, and the factored-quadratic synthesis.

root_causes.description: The coverage contract is written per PROBLEM, not per printed RESPONSE SLOT. One entry discharges a problem id no matter how many separate things the item asks the student to write, so problem 5's remainder and the three one-sentence explanations pass through a fully green gate chain.
evidence: SKILL.md:189 — 'verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check (use `manual` for the unverifiable ones), so a partially-verified answer key can never slip through'. The trailing promise does not follow from the rule: the rule counts PROBLEMS, the promise is about ANSWERS.
scripts/verify.py:2020 — the coverage gate is `missing = [i for i in range(1, problem_count + 1) if i not in ids]`, i.e. membership of the id set, never a count of printed response slots

tests/check_layout.py:47-49 and ANSWER_RE at :99 — the layout gate requires that each item CONTAIN one answer-location macro; it never compares that count against the number of verify entries carrying the id
worksheet.tex problem 5 prints two demands against one verify entry (id 5, eval I**18 -> -1)
gate_log.txt ends '✅ BUILD PASSED — all gates green' with verify-ws PASS

root_causes.description: SKILL.md gives two instructions about `manual` that pull in opposite directions, and the rationing one wins. An author writing a fluency sheet reads 'Reserve manual for genuinely open reasoning' and concludes that a single explanatory sentence attached to an otherwise computational problem does not earn an entry — which is precisely how problems 6, 7 and 12 ended up with none.
evidence: SKILL.md:249 — 'Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning (proofs, "explain why", construction)'. 'Reserve' is rationing language and is what an author follows when deciding a single sentence is not worth a manual entry.

SKILL.md:257 — 'Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, Riemann sum tables, series convergence arguments, and any explanation/reasoning answer.' This clause is broad and correct, and it is the one that is being ignored.
Neither line is enforced: no gate reads the worksheet prose for an imperative like 'explain', 'say in one sentence', 'name the error' or 'state whether'
worksheet.tex problems 6, 7 and 12 each append 'say in one sentence why/what' to a computational stem; verify.json declares no manual entry for any of them

improvements.title: Every printed response slot needs its own verification entry, not one per problem
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule from 'one check per problem id' to 'one check per printed response slot'. Concretely: (a) rewrite SKILL.md:189 so the promise matches the rule — require an entry for every distinct thing the item asks the student to write, and delete the 'a partially-verified answer key can never slip through' clause until the rule can support it; (b) extend tests/check_layout.py to count response demands inside each \problem segment (answer-location macros plus imperative clauses such as 'State the', 'Write the', 'List each') and fail when that count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying the id. The schema already permits several entries per id — problem 12 uses two — so problem 5 simply needs a second entry, {"id": 5, "type": "eval", "expr": "Mod(n, 4)", "at": {"n": 18}, "expected": 2}, which is an exactly checkable value the key already prints.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints an \ansblank plus a second 'State the remainder:' demand, paired with a verify JSON carrying a single entry for id 1; assert check_layout.py exits non-zero and names problem 1. Today it exits 0, which is the defect.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores binding for the response the topic actually turns on. Problem 5 is the sheet's only pure powers-of-i item, and the remainder is the mechanism the directions box teaches ('Divide the exponent by 4 and keep the remainder'); today it is the one printed answer with nothing behind it.
improvements.risk: Medium. A clause-based slot counter will initially fire on hint sentences that read like demands ('Remember that squaring a binomial means multiplying it by itself' in problem 8 is not a response demand). Land it warn-only for one run, tune against the existing eval corpus, then make it a hard gate.

improvements.title: Written explanations the worksheet demands are recorded as machine-verified rather than manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a prose scan and a hard gate. In tests/check_layout.py, match a small set of open-response imperatives inside each \problem segment — 'say in one sentence', 'explain', 'why', 'describe', 'justify', 'state whether' — and require that the matching problem id carry at least one entry of type `manual`. Then collapse SKILL.md:249 and :257 into one unambiguous rule: any printed demand for an explanation, a diagnosis, a named error or a drawn mark gets a `manual` entry IN ADDITION to whatever computational entries the problem carries. Here that means three new manual entries, for ids 6, 7 and 12, each carrying the reviewer criterion the answer key already spells out.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem whose stem is 'Simplify (5+2i)(5-2i). Then say in one sentence why the answer has no imaginary part.' with a verify JSON holding only an eval for that id; assert check_layout.py exits non-zero citing the unflagged explanation. Silent today.
improvements.expected_impact: Turns this sheet from '0 manual, all verified' into '12 verified plus 3 flagged', which is the honest statement. It also makes the exit-2 manual-review path fire, so the delivery message stops claiming 'Nothing is flagged manual' on a sheet with three written explanations.
improvements.risk: Medium. Keyword matching will over-fire on directions boxes and on hint clauses containing 'why' rhetorically. Scope the scan to \problem segments only, exclude the preamble, and ship warn-only first.

improvements.title: Integer answers print with an ASCII hyphen while the neighbouring symbolic answers use a real minus sign
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, `_fmt()` returns bare `str(v)` for the int/Decimal branch and `repr(v)` for floats, so a negative number reaches LaTeX as text-mode '-3'. Every string expected, by contrast, goes through `sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v))` and gets a proper math-mode minus. Wrap the numeric branches in math mode the same way — return '$' + str(v) + '$' (Decimal formatting is preserved because the string is built before the wrap, so a verified 6.30 still prints 6.30). Do it for int, Decimal and float alike.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py rendering a verify JSON with {"id": 1, "expected": -3} and {"id": 2, "expected": "x - 7"}, and assert both rendered entries contain the same minus token (i.e. entry 1 is '$-3$', not the bare '-3'). It fails today: entry 1 renders '-3' in text mode and entry 2 renders '$x - 7$'.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a visible inconsistency inside a single bank. In this slice alone it shows in curr-352 ('5. -1' beside '8. 7 - 24i'), curr-363, curr-369, curr-382, curr-388 and curr-400.
improvements.risk: Low. The bank is plain text by design and is never read by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem answer-key binding cannot be affected. The only failure mode is a LaTeX compile error, which the existing compile-ak gate catches on the same run.

case_summary: Mathematically this is a clean sheet: twelve complex-number results, all independently recomputed and all matching the key, with a real difficulty ramp and no repeated skeleton. The rejection is the shard's dominant defect. Problem 5 asks for a value and a remainder and verifies only the value; problems 6, 7 and 12 each append a one-sentence explanation to a computational stem and none is declared manual; the gate chain reports zero manual items and final_response.md repeats that as a virtue. The missing data is not hard to produce — the answer key already prints the remainder (18 = 4*4+2) and model sentences for all three explanations. Only the verify.json declaration is absent. Beyond the judge's finding, the Quick Answers bank prints '5. -1' with a text-mode hyphen beside '8. 7 - 24i' with a real minus.
